patch.value: GH-1605: Preserve recent events when default history output must be bounded

**Version:** pm 2026.10.26, non-git tracker, one item with 251 history entries (two concurrent writers, 50 ops each).

**Repro**
```sh
pm history <id>              # default
pm history <id> --limit 5    # "Latest n entries"
```
**Observed:** the default read renders entries **1–183** oldest-first, hits the output ceiling and returns `has_more: true, truncated: true`; the **68 newest entries — including the latest handoff/update — are not in the answer**. It costs 15,960 bytes. `--limit 5` returns entries 247–251 in 815 bytes.

**Expected:** when the default history read must truncate, it should keep the newest entries (and point to the cursor for older ones), or default to a bounded recent window with an explicit way to page back to the start. History verification itself is fine (all 251 entries verify); this is only about which end of the timeline survives truncation.

**Why it matters for agents:** "what happened last on this item?" is the normal handoff question. With the current default an agent spends ~16 KB of context on the oldest events and still needs a second call to see the current state — about 95% of the bytes are avoidable for that question.


Intake boundary: this is a report against published 2026.10.26, not proof of a current-checkout defect. Reproduce in an external sandbox before implementation. Related completed work retains its shipped scope. Proposed examples or categories are not accepted contracts until validated.

Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1605

Reproduce the reported 251-entry timeline in an external non-Git tracker and measure the selected entries and rendered bytes.; A bounded default keeps the most recent events with correct original numbering, complete counts and executable older-page recovery; explicit full reads preserve complete chronological history.; SDK, CLI and MCP selection and continuation semantics remain consistent, with no duplicate or skipped entries and no change to integrity verification.
The ordinary recent-history question retains the latest handoff within its budget and offers explicit, lossless continuation to older entries.
